主要内容: General Motors (GM) reported Q4 2021 earnings that beat Wall Street expectations, with adjusted earnings per share of $1.35, exceeding the $1.19 expected. The company expects an operating profit of $13 billion to $15 billion for 2022, in line with analyst forecasts. GM noted improvements in semiconductor supply, which had impacted production and sales in 2021. CEO Mary Barra emphasized accelerating its $35 billion investment in electric and autonomous vehicles through 2025. The company plans to use saved capital for these investments rather than reinstating its dividend, which was cut during the pandemic. North American operations contributed the most to profits in 2021, generating over $10.3 billion. GM's financial arm generated over $5 billion in 2021, including about $1.2 billion in Q4. International operations earned $827 million, including $275 million in Q4. The company spent about $1.2 billion on its majority-owned autonomous vehicle subsidiary, Cruise, in 2021. GM aims to become the top seller of EVs in the U.S. by 2025, with plans to increase EV production capacity in North America to 1 million units by that time frame.
